label: C-03
title: Antimatter inherits single-step OpenZeppelin Ownable rather than Ownable2Step
titleNote: SHORTENED. The classifier's title carried the mistyped-transferOwnership consequence ('so a mistyped transferOwnership permanently loses every owner power the protocol depends on'); that clause is struck - see strippedAttackPath.
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Newly minted this run; verified to reproduce from fingerprintBasis and not to collide with any of the 19 pre-existing ledger fingerprints.
originNote: origin 'new' means NEW TO THE LEDGER (first time filed), NOT new to the code. See regressionStatement.

qaBundleText.note: WHAT SURVIVES INTO THE QA BUNDLE IS TWO LINES. Nothing more should be written up.
qaBundleText.line2: Combined with C-02 (3a90280bed325637, no local pause authority), every incident lever the protocol has runs through one owner key whose transfer has no undo.

strippedAttackPath.authority: validity-checker (VALID-IF-RESCOPED; carve-out 'admin-mistake' DETECTED, scoped to the attack-path narrative) + severity-auditor. BINDING.
removed: 1. Owner calls transferOwnership(addr) with a mistyped, unowned, or non-signing address.
2. OpenZeppelin's single-step Ownable transfers immediately - there is no acceptOwnership step and no undo.
3. All owner-gated functions are permanently unreachable.
strippedAttackPath.alsoRemoved: The 'permanently loses every owner power the protocol depends on' framing, from the title and from the impact statement.
strippedAttackPath.reason: THAT CONSEQUENCE IS OBVIOUS AND HITS THE RECKLESS-ADMIN CARVE-OUT. No competent owner is surprised that mistyping an address in transferOwnership hands over the contract, so it fails the Law-3 surprise test and must not be presented as a hazard scenario. Declining the escalation does not license withholding the finding (Law 1 forbids that), which is why the structural observation is retained and filed at QA.
strippedAttackPath.whatSurvives: The structural C-02 MULTIPLIER, and only that: every incident lever the protocol has runs through a single owner key whose transfer has no undo. That is a centralization observation about the protocol's shape, not an incident story about a typo, and it survives the carve-out.

classification.assetImpact: No direct impact and no attacker. Structural: Antimatter's owner-gated surface (setPhUSD, setPhUSDMinter, setApprovedMinter, stablecoin registration decisions, rescueERC20) is reachable only through a single key, and the transfer of that key has no acceptance step.
classification.attackPathNote: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. No attacker participates and the owner-error narrative was struck as an obvious admin mistake - see strippedAttackPath.
classification.likelihood: n/a - a structural centralization observation, not an exploit path.
classification.externalRequirements: None - which is also why it is not a security finding.

regressionStatement: EXPLICITLY NOT A REGRESSION, AND NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS DELTA. VERIFIED: `Ownable` traces to the repository's initial commit a94fd72, and the 0bb82d8..c91bc1a diff does not touch the import at :8 or the inheritance at :22. This is a RUN-01 COVERAGE GAP surfaced by the 4naly3er repair between runs - 4naly3er and Semgrep did not run in run-01 - not a defect introduced by c91bc1a. Any downstream stage that files it as a regression, or attributes it to c91bc1a, is wrong. The `regression: false` field is load-bearing and must be preserved.
c4Criterion: QA/Low - 'Governance/Centralization risk including admin privileges'. The definitional case. It cannot reach Medium or High: no attacker participates and no asset moves.
law3Verdict: TRUSTED-OWNER TERRITORY FOR THE ESCALATION, FILED AT QA REGARDLESS. The footgun half fails the Law-3 surprise test - the consequence of mistyping an address in transferOwnership is obvious - so it does not qualify as a submission-grade operational hazard and its narrative is struck. That declines the escalation only; it does not license withholding the finding, which Law 1 forbids.
justification: QA, on two independent grounds that both CAP rather than suppress. First, C4 places governance and admin-privilege matters in QA by definition. Second, this is a common automated-tool finding with no demonstrated H/M exploit path, which C4 discounts - but that applies AS A SEVERITY CEILING ONLY, never as a suppression: Law 1 says cull noise at /ledger triage, not by withholding it from the scan. Its practical weight is entirely as a multiplier on ledger C-02 (Antimatter has no kill switch of its own): every incident lever this protocol has runs through an owner key whose transfer has no undo, and the open High H-01 is a one-transaction theft that Antimatter's own owner already has no proportionate lever to stop. Cheap to fix, so worth fixing; not worth more than QA. A reasonable /ledger triage outcome is wont-fix - that is a human call, not an audit-stage one.
recommendation: Inherit Ownable2Step instead of Ownable so ownership transfer requires the incoming owner to call acceptOwnership. One-line change, no behavioural cost, and it composes with the incident-response runbook C-02 already asks for.

notes.relatedTo: C-02 (3a90280bed325637, no local pause authority) - a multiplier on it, not a duplicate of it.

evidence.provenanceVerification: git log traces `import {Ownable}` and `contract Antimatter is ERC20, Ownable` to initial commit a94fd72; `git diff 0bb82d8..c91bc1a -- src/Antimatter.sol` does not touch lines 8 or 22.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues authority on this project. The tool-noise carve-out applies AS A SEVERITY CEILING ONLY, not as a suppression (Law 1: cull at triage, never withhold from the scan). Not filed as a regression.

carveOutsConsidered: common findings from automated tools without a demonstrated H/M exploit path
validityCheck.toolFindingRuling: DETECTED - SEVERITY CEILING, NOT SUPPRESSION. 4naly3er L-2 / L-12, the canonical example of the category. C4 also places governance/centralization in QA by definition, and Ownable2Step is a routine QA line item in real C4 QA reports.
validityCheck.adminMistakeRuling: DETECTED, SCOPED TO THE ATTACK-PATH NARRATIVE ONLY. Stripped - see strippedAttackPath.
validityCheck.verdictScope: INVALID as a standalone submission and INVALID as a Law-3 operational hazard; VALID as bundled QA.
validityCheck.provenanceUpheld: regression=false is CORRECT and must be preserved.
validityCheck.recommendation: Keep at QA in the bundle with the narrowed framing.
